metadata.note: The Carolina and North-Western Railway (1895-1974) and its predecessors: the broad-gauge Kings Mountain Railroad (Chester - Yorkville SC, 1850s, dead after the Civil War), the 3 ft gauge Chester and Lenoir Narrow Gauge Railroad (Chester SC - Lenoir NC, opened in stages 1875-1884, 'the largest narrow gauge railroad in the Carolinas'), and the Caldwell and Northern (Lenoir - Collettsville - Edgemont). The C&NW bought the C&L at foreclosure on 8 Feb 1897, standard-gauged it in 1902, bought the C&N on 1 Jul 1910, ran the Edgemont Branch for passengers to 1937 and the main line to 1947. Southern Railway controlled it by stock but it kept its own name, timetable and trains until it became the (second) Norfolk Southern Railway on 1 Jan 1974, so Southern control is not a Rule 4 split. Rule 4 splits drawn: C&L | Richmond and Danville (lease, 1886-1893) | C&L receivers (1893-1897) | C&NW (from 1897); Caldwell and Northern | C&NW (1910). LineString-only geometry: because the 9.2 mi Newton - Hickory link (Southern trackage rights) is drawn only from 1902, every pre-1902 era is two features (Chester - Newton and Hickory - Lenoir), and the C&NW 1902-1947 main line is three features (Chester - Newton, Newton - Hickory, Hickory - Lenoir).

metadata.tracer_decisions: Applied 2026-11-05 on the requester's instructions for the report's open questions: (1) lease era split as Chester and Lenoir to 1886 | Richmond and Danville 1886-1893 | Chester and Lenoir (receivers) 1893-1897, each C&L block keeping its own opening year; the Charlotte Columbia & Augusta lease (c.1883/84-1886) is not drawn as an era. (2) Newton - Hickory trackage rights drawn only 1902-1947, as its own C&NW feature. (3) Main line ends 1947 (secondary sources), Edgemont Branch 1937, Kings Mountain RR 1858 [ANCHOR], Caldwell and Northern 1906-1910 then C&NW Edgemont Branch 1910-1937. (4) Nothing dropped silently - see omitted.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) LEASE ERA: the 1886 and 1893 Richmond & Danville boundaries rest on a trovestar catalogue blurb and a CRHA newsletter (not read in full) - medium-low confidence. The Charlotte, Columbia & Augusta lease that preceded it (c.1883-84 to 1886, start date unsourced) is NOT drawn as its own era; those years stay in Chester and Lenoir colour. Whether CC&A or R&D is the right operator 1884-1886 is open. (2) NEWTON - HICKORY 1884-1902: how 3 ft gauge trains used the 9.2 mi of standard-gauge WNC/R&D/Southern track (third rail, or a change of trains at Newton) is not established, so the link is drawn only from 1902 and the pre-1902 C&L, R&D and C&NW features leave a geometry gap between Newton and Hickory. (3) MAIN LINE END 1947 rests on three secondary sources (wvncrails, Wikipedia, tarheelpress) that may share an origin; the latest cited timetable is 1941; a Hickory Daily Record / Gastonia Gazette / Lenoir News-Topic search for 1946-1948 or an NCUC / SC PSC order would settle it. Mixed trains 1947-1951 are unknown (the 1952 Guide rules out public service by Sep 1951). (4) KINGS MOUNTAIN RR [ANCHOR] 1858 only: opening year (1850s; 'construction began 1855' vs the 1848 charter), end of service in the Civil War and the gauge are all unsourced beyond secondary statements. (5) OPENINGS: Gastonia 1876 (wvncrails) vs state line - Lincolnton 1880 (ICC) - drawn 1880; Lincolnton 1880 (ICC) vs July 1881 (wvncrails) - drawn 1881; Lincolnton - Newton 1883 (wvncrails) vs 2 June 1884 (ICC) - drawn 1884; Lenoir 17 May vs 2 June 1884. Dallas never separately dated. (6) CALDWELL AND NORTHERN: no positive evidence of passenger trains before the 1906 Guide; the 1906 start is a first-proven year, not a known start; C&N-named trains to Edgemont 1906-1910 rest on wvncrails alone. (7) EDGEMONT BRANCH END: 1937 (passenger, wvncrails) vs 1938 (abandonment, last train into Edgemont, passengers not stated). (8) All headways and speeds are estimates. (9) Geometry: about 26 mi of the Chester - Lincolnton grade and 9.3 mi of the Edgemont Branch are straight-line legs, and 11.3 mi of the branch is drawn along Wilson Creek as a stand-in (see each feature's geometry_quality).
metadata.omitted: Charlotte, Columbia & Augusta lease era (c.1883/84-1886): not drawn as its own era (start date unsourced; requester's decision) - covered by Chester and Lenoir features. Newton - Hickory 1884-1902: not drawn (see not_yet_sourced 2). Chester and Lenoir Yorkville - Gastonia 1876-1879 and Dallas - Lincolnton 1880: withheld under the report's confirmed-only drawable spans (the earlier dates conflict with the ICC valuation). Main line 1948-1951: no passenger evidence; freight only by Sep 1951 (Rule 1). Edgemont Branch 1938: abandonment-year 'last train', passengers not stated. Northampton & Hertford (Gumberry - Jackson NC): Wikipedia attributes it to the C&NW in 1917, but the ICC valuation and Fowler give it to the Carolina and NorthEASTERN - not a C&NW line, not drawn. Southern-system short lines administered under the C&NW from the early 1950s (Yadkin RR, High Point Randleman Asheboro & Southern, Danville and Western...): the C&NW never ran passenger trains on them. Queen City Coach Co. buses honouring C&NW tickets Lenoir - Hickory (1952 Guide): a bus, not rail. Wikipedia's 1943 Chester - Edgemont train: inconsistent with the 1938 abandonment, not used. Conover, Cliffs, Rhodhiss and the other stations: no station layer entries were made (none of these lines is in data/stations/).
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Whole C&NW after the 1947 end of passenger service (Feb 1952 Guide: '(FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY)'); post-1947 freight on Chester - York (to c.1972), York - Clover (1981), Newton - Lincolnton (c.1990), Gastonia - Dallas (2003); Hickory - Lenoir as the Caldwell County Railroad from 1994; Edgemont Branch 1938 dismantling trains.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. Fowler's South Carolina file (line 67) tags the intermediate stops Poor House, Lowrysville, Sandy River Road, District Line, Guthriesville and Philadelphia with the 1858 Dinsmore Guide letter, so trains were advertised in 1858. Do not widen this anchor without a dated timetable. Broad (5 ft) gauge feeder off the Charlotte & South Carolina at Chester; its right-of-way was reused by the Chester and Lenoir in 1874-75.
